content: {"rule":"K-S2","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge text enters an UNDERDETERMINED verdict and states the ground for it, so K-S2's restriction on grounds for UNDERDETERMINED is applicable.","verdict":"CLEAN","quote":"D5 vs C1 (Acts 2:30): UNDERDETERMINED -- [CR2] and [CR3] answered the loins/seed row with Genesis 46:26 and Hebrews 7:10 (loins at depth) and the legal/flesh distinction, while [DR3] presses that the only named Davidic man is Joseph; neither chain forces the other.","rule_words":"That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.","room":"The phrase 'That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground' could be read narrowly as barring only an explicit single-verse silence ground, or broadly as barring any underdetermination involving a non-stated link; I weighed these readings.","why":"The judge's stated ground is that neither chain forces the other, not that a single verse fails to state the link or its contrary."}
